class.name: FellowVehicleDamage3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: a vehicle's body dented where it hits.
class.description: A child of a [FellowVehicle3D]. It turns the vehicle's contact reporting on ([member RigidBody3D.contact_monitor], at least 8 [member RigidBody3D.max_contacts_reported]) and reads the body's contacts every physics step: when their impulses together exceed [member impulse_threshold], each contact pushes the vertices of the vehicle's meshes within [member radius] of it into the body (along its normal, towards the body's centre of mass), [member softness] metres for each N·s beyond the threshold, falling off smoothly to the radius's edge; no vertex moves more than [member max_depth] from where it was. The dented meshes are copies made at the first impact (the originals are kept: [method repair]); their normals are recomputed from the dented triangles. The meshes are those of [member mesh_paths], or without them every [MeshInstance3D] of the vehicle but those of its wheels. A mesh with blend shapes is left as it is. The collision shapes are not changed. See [code]docs/decisions/0213-vehicle-damage.md[/code]. The dents can also reach the running gear (both off by default): a wheel near a dent is bent out of line ([member wheel_bend]: the vehicle pulls to one side) and an engine the dent reaches loses power ([member engine_power_loss]). An impact reaches into the body twice as far as it spreads over it: [member radius] across the push, twice that along it. See [code]docs/decisions/0215-running-gear-damage.md[/code]. [codeblock] var damage = FellowVehicleDamage3D.new() car.add_child(damage) damage.impacted.connect(func(position, impulse, depth): print("dented ", depth, " m")) [/codeblock]

method.name: apply_impact
method.description: Dents the body as an impact would (an explosion's blast, a scripted crash): at [param position] (global), pushed along [param direction] (into the body), as deep as an impulse of [param impulse] N·s makes it. Below [member impulse_threshold] nothing happens.

method.name: get_damage
method.description: The deepest dent as a share of [member max_depth] (0-1): for the game's damage model (the engine's power, the steering's pull, a smoking bonnet).

method.name: get_deepest_dent
method.description: The largest distance any vertex has moved, in metres.

method.name: get_engine_power
method.description: The share of the engine's torque left (1 undamaged): see [member engine_power_loss].

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Diagnostics: [code]impacts[/code], [code]deepest[/code], [code]damage[/code], [code]deform_usec[/code] (the time spent denting), [code]meshes[/code], [code]dented_meshes[/code], [code]vertices[/code] (of the meshes copied).

method.name: get_vertex_offset
method.description: How far a vertex of a mesh (its path from this node) has been dented, in the mesh's space.

method.name: get_wheel_toe_change
method.description: How far the dents have bent a wheel's [member FellowWheel3D.toe] (its path from this node), in degrees (+ in).

method.name: repair
method.description: Puts the original meshes back and forgets the dents.

members.member: Where the engine is, in the vehicle's space (the default: a front-engined car about 4 m long, its origin in the middle, its front towards -Z).

The share of the engine's torque ([member FellowVehicle3D.max_torque]) lost when a dent of [member max_depth] reaches [member engine_position] (less for a shallower dent or one farther off). 0: the engine is never hurt. [method repair] gives it back (unless the game has changed [member FellowVehicle3D.max_torque] since).

The impulse (N·s) the body's contacts must exceed in one physics step before it dents: below it bumps, kerbs, pushes and a 1 400 kg car meeting a wall at 5 km/h (about 1 700 N·s a step) leave it as it is; at 30 km/h the wall takes about 6 600 N·s in its first step.
The farthest a vertex is moved from where it was, in metres, however many impacts.
The meshes to dent (paths from this node). Empty: every [MeshInstance3D] of the vehicle but its wheels'.
How far from a contact the body is dented, in metres.
Metres of dent for each N·s of impulse beyond [member impulse_threshold] (2e-5: about 10 cm at 30 km/h for a 1 400 kg car).

The most a dent can bend a wheel's [member FellowWheel3D.toe], in degrees. A dent reaching a wheel turns it about its upright the way the push would: a push from the side ahead of the wheel's centre turns its front in, one from the front outside the centre turns it out, as far as the dent is deep (up to this at [member max_depth] and close to the wheel). A wheel out of line makes the vehicle pull to one side with the steering straight. 0: the wheels are never bent. [method repair] puts them back.

signal.name: impacted
signal.description: An impact dented the body: where (global), its impulse (N·s) and the dent's depth at its centre (m).
